title: Privacy
metaTitle: Privacy Policy | Colorado Mineral Rights Buyer
metaDescription: How we collect, use, and protect information you share with us about your Colorado mineral or royalty interest, including documents and contact details.
heroLead: This page explains what information we collect when you reach out about a mineral interest, how we use it, and how it's protected.
intro: When you contact us about a Colorado mineral or royalty interest, you may share personal and property information, including your name, contact details, county and legal description information, and copies of documents like deeds, division orders, or royalty statements. This policy describes how we handle that information.
We collect only what's reasonably needed to evaluate an interest and communicate with you about it, and we don't sell your personal information to third parties for marketing purposes.

sections.heading: Information we collect
paragraphs: This typically includes your name, phone number, email address, mailing address, and details about the mineral or royalty interest you're inquiring about, such as county, legal description, decimal interest, and any documents you choose to share, like deeds, division orders, or royalty statements. If you submit a form on our site, we collect the information entered into that form.

We may also collect basic technical information automatically when you visit our site, such as browser type, general location derived from IP address, and pages viewed, through standard analytics tools. This helps us understand how the site is used and doesn't identify you personally unless combined with information you've separately provided.

sections.heading: How we use your information
paragraphs: We use the information you provide to evaluate your mineral interest, prepare an offer, communicate with you about the process, and, if you proceed with a sale, complete the necessary title review and closing steps. We may also use it to respond to questions you've asked, even if unrelated to a sale.

We do not use your information for purposes unrelated to evaluating your interest or communicating with you without your knowledge. If we ever needed to use it differently, we'd seek your consent first.

sections.heading: How we share information
paragraphs: We may share relevant information with title companies, county recording offices, or operators of record as a normal part of completing a title review or closing a transaction, since this information is necessary to verify ownership and process a sale. We do not sell your personal information to third-party marketers.
We may disclose information if required by law, such as in response to a valid subpoena or court order, or to protect our legal rights in a dispute.

sections.heading: Data retention and your choices
paragraphs: We retain information for as long as reasonably necessary to complete an evaluation or transaction and to satisfy any applicable legal, tax, or recordkeeping obligations. If you'd like your contact information removed from future communications, or have questions about what we hold, you can reach out and we'll address the request.
If you choose not to share certain documents or details, that's understandable, though it may limit how precise an initial evaluation can be until that information is available.

sections.heading: Security measures
paragraphs: We use reasonable administrative and technical safeguards to protect information you share with us, including limiting access to personal and document information to those who need it to evaluate your interest or process a transaction. That said, no method of transmitting or storing information electronically is completely secure, and we can't guarantee absolute security.

If you're sending sensitive documents like a deed or a royalty statement, use whatever method you're most comfortable with, and let us know if you'd prefer a specific secure channel rather than standard email.

sections.heading: Children's privacy and policy updates
paragraphs: This site and our services are directed at adult mineral owners, not children, and we don't knowingly collect information from minors. If we become aware that we've received information from a minor without appropriate consent, we'll take steps to delete it.

We may update this privacy policy periodically to reflect changes in our practices or applicable law. The version posted here is the current one, and continued use of our site or services after an update means you accept the revised policy.

faqs.question: Do you sell my personal information to third parties?
faqs.answer: No, we don't sell your personal information for marketing purposes. Information is shared only as needed with title companies, county offices, or operators to complete a transaction.

faqs.question: What happens to my documents if I don't move forward with a sale?
faqs.answer: We retain information only as long as reasonably needed and you can request that your contact details be removed from future outreach at any time.

faqs.question: Is my information kept secure?
faqs.answer: We take reasonable measures to protect information you share with us, though no method of electronic storage or transmission is completely secure.

faqs.question: Can I ask what information you have about me?
faqs.answer: Yes, reach out through our contact page and we'll address requests about what information we hold and how it's being used.

faqs.question: Do you use cookies or tracking on your website?
faqs.answer: We may use standard analytics tools to understand general site usage, which typically doesn't identify you personally on its own.

faqs.question: Will you contact me after I submit a form even if I don't respond?
faqs.answer: We may follow up on an inquiry you've submitted, but you can ask us to stop contacting you at any time, and we'll honor that request.

faqs.question: How do I request that my information be deleted?
faqs.answer: Reach out through our contact page with your request, and we'll address it, subject to any documents we're required to retain for legal or recordkeeping purposes.
